{"self_assessment": "Impact
I built the belly line (stroke 2), the lower half of the fish's outline. I laid it from the nose join in several steady batches, and it carried the fall the whole way to the low point of the belly. Before the push, the whole run of 125 dominoes traced as connected from the start. The belly is a large part of the outline the judge sees, so it matters for recognising the fish.

Execution
I began the belly as soon as the back line reached the nose, so the fall passed cleanly from one stroke to the next. I stopped at the agreed low point so Hana could carry on from there without overlap. After laying it, I inspected the area closely four times (around the middle join, the doubled patch and the back near the head). Each time I confirmed the run was connected and nothing needed patching. I also noticed the doubled bit on the back and checked it was still connected.

Collaboration
I proposed splitting the work so that no two people were on the same stroke, which kept hands from colliding. I stayed clear of Hana's tail stretch, and I asked Jack and Omar to cover specific checks. When the doubled bit came up, I asked about it directly and then recommended leaving it alone. Once the build was done I kept my hands off the table so nothing got bumped before the push.

Leadership
I took charge of how the belly work was split and made sure everyone knew who owned which stretch. I kept the table coordinated on the plan: build, verify, then hands off. In the last minutes I helped keep the team calm and focused on leaving the connected run undisturbed.", "my_share_percent": 30}
